issues.description: The problem statement and UML require Farm.animals to be a List<Animal> (initialized as an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor) to preserve insertion order and follow the specified aggregation. The solution implementation uses a Set<Animal> (HashSet) for the animals field and initializes it accordingly. This changes collection semantics (no ordering guarantee, different duplicate handling) and can alter observable behavior such as the order of verses printed by singFarmSong(), conflicting with the explicit instruction to use an ArrayList.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification: change the Farm.animals type to List<Animal> and initialize it with new ArrayList<>() in the no-arg constructor. Update the getter/setter signatures and implementations to use List<Animal>, and retain iteration over the list in singFarmSong() and feedAllAnimals() so insertion order and intended song output are preserved. Alternatively, if unordered semantics were intended, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly specify a Set and explain implications.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly specify that Farm should aggregate animals using a List (and instruct to initialize an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor), while the provided solution implements the Farm.animals attribute as a Set (HashSet) and exposes getters/setters returning Set<Animal>. This is a mismatch in the expected collection type for the same conceptual entity 'the farm's animals' and changes semantics (ordering, duplicates) and the API students are asked to implement, creating confusion when mapping requirements to implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem statement and template by using List<Animal> as the type for the animals attribute and initialize it as an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor. Update getter/setter signatures to return and accept List<Animal> and ensure addAnimal and other methods operate on a List. Alternatively, if a Set is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to explicitly require a Set to avoid mismatch.
